steps.content: You and OwO look around the abandoned village and knock on almost every one of the dusty doors, but you don't find any trace of life here.
Bagley doesn't follow you into the village. Perhaps he can't bear ruining those only memories he holds, he just stays outside the village, squatting there and guarding those flowers.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Bagley...
Even OwO, who's always bubbly, doesn't know how to break it to Bagley that no one lives in his village anymore. She can only hold the lion head and slump beside Bagley.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: OwO, I'm sorry...
Just when OwO is still debating how to tell Bagley, the boy stares at the flowers blankly and begins.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: If it's about stealing the lion's head, forget it. I've gotten over it.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: No... I shouldn't have called you a liar... The lion head's power indeed exists.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: But... But it seems like OwO didn't help you find anything at all.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: It's not your fault. It's not the lion head's fault either. Just that my home...
Bagley's shoulders shake dejectedly, his teardrops landing on the violet petals.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Eh, s-s-stop crying!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Maybe they've just moved somewhere else and haven't got the time to find you yet!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Look, there isn't even a drop of water around here. This is no place to live in!
OwO is used to receiving consolation but has never consoled others before, so her improvised excuse is pretty clumsy.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I was sent away to DisCity to escape the disaster. Where else could they have moved to other than DisCity? Why haven't they come look for me? Why has no one told me anything...
Whimpering, Bagley refutes OwO's flimsy assumption.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I don't need your pity... There are no disasters to hide from in OwO's home. You came back to DisCity because you like it here. They're both your homes. But it's different for me...

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I don't like DisCity! I just want to go home, even more than you do. This place is all I have, but...
A little stupefied, he looks up at the sandy wind decaying his birthplace, and his tears overflow uncontrollably.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: But even this place is no more...
OwO follows Bagley's gaze and looks toward the empty village, still a little bewildered.
Even though she has pushed open every door in there and witnessed up close the desolation and silence, she still can't comprehend Bagley's sadness.
Her home in DisCity will always welcome her with the heater and snacks, and every family in Goldionville has warmly received the girl who protected the caravan.
Indeed, she doesn't understand what it's like to lose her home. Getting ambushed by the bearded men trying to snatch Starbeast is already the biggest challenge she's ever faced in her life.
But she can somehow understand... Back then in DisCity, when she stood alone and watched the other kids, she understood that the congested feeling that made her want to cry was called loneliness.
OwO turns back and walks toward you sullenly, burying her head into your coat.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Can't! Do! It! OwO can't cheer him up. Who knows there's something even the lion dance genius can't achieve?
Should the little clapper go and clean up the mess now?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Don't make me ask!
OwO's voice sounds dull and she seems sulky.
I know a way to cheer him up, but I shouldn't be the one doing it.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Why?
OwO looks up from your coat, the tip of her nose still red.
Because he's OwO's friend.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: ...OwO's friend.
She repeats the words a few times, then finally nods firmly.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: That's right, OwO should do it!
She rubs her face on your coat again. Once she collects herself, she holds out a hand to you palm up and lifts it twice.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Tell me how!
The sandy wind has dried Bagley's tears. With two pale tear stains on his face, he sits beside the violet flowers and stares blankly at the village far ahead.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I know a story about your village. Want to hear it?
The chatty girl hovers over to sit beside Bagley again. Bagley doesn't answer.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: No answer means yes!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Did you know this flower is called pearly? Does this name ring any bells with you?

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I've heard of it before...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Because Pearly is also the name of this village!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: That sounds... right.
Bagley can't remember it very clearly.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: That's right, pearlies are unique to this village. They've grown here since a long, long time ago.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Not only are they beautiful, but they are also the raw material of a useful dye!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: The villagers introduced this dye to DisCity, and DisCity introduced it to the rest of the world.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Even now, pearlies are used to make colorings in many places!
Bagley seems a bit bewildered by this information about his home. He never knew that this tiny flower he held so close to his heart grew in other places as well.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Goldionville was named after the big golden lion who guarded the village and brought good auspices.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: People from your village must have named the village after these tiny flowers because pearlies brought them hope! That's the tradition and culture of your village!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Pearlies, and the Pearly village...
Bagley keeps repeating this strange yet familiar name a little glumly, touching the fragile petals tentatively.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It was the hope of the village, and it will be your hope too!
OwO grabs Bagley's hand and guides him to touch the petals boldly.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: See, your touch won't damage it! It may look shriveled, but it's in fact very tough! Look how it survives this harsh environment and lives on with everyone's hope!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Pearlies are super tough flowers! The Pearly village is a super awesome dye manufacturer!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: The whole world uses this dye... Which means... like me, there must be some people traveled to different parts of the world, with this flower!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Wherever there's the pearly dye, there are pearlies and the hope of the Pearly village!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Exactly! The hope of the Pearly village is everywhere! Your home is not gone, it's only turned into these pearlies and now they bloom in many different places in the world!
The two kids get excited with the talk and both stand up to take a better look at this ancient village.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Do the flowers remember the villagers?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Of course they do! Just like OwO's lion head must remember OwO!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Then do they remember my mom and dad too?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Yes! OwO's lion head was passed on to me from my great-great-great-grandfather. It remembers everything!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: How do I find these flowers in DisCity?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Find them? Aren't they right here before you? We can bring them back and grow them ourselves!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Do you remember what you asked me? If it's so nice back home, why did I come back to DisCity?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You're right. I like it there. I like the people there! I like the neighbors, Deren, and little clapper!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Although I left home, I don't feel lonely at all!
OwO smiles at you and pats the lion head in her arms.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: The lion head is the seed of Goldionville. Wherever OwO brings it to is home!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: If I want it to be DisCity, then DisCity it'll be...
OwO dances with the lion head on the sand, screaming recklessly. Her shrill, childish laughter blends into the sandy wind, somehow turning into a pleasant sound.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: DisCity it'll be. I'll take it back to DisCity.
Bagley carefully digs out a whole pearly plant from the sand and cups it in his palms.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I must plant the pearly in a sunny place.
They laugh and play, chasing each other in this desolate desert. You only begin to head back once these two little ones are both completely exhausted.
In the rear-view mirror, you see the two of them try to stay up and bicker despite their sleepy eyes, one holding the flower and the other hugging the lion head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: My lion dance is no doubt cooler than your dye.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: You literally just lost your lion head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Mind your attitude when you talk to the genius pretty lion dancer. I may consider teaching you a move or two if I'm in a good mood.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: As if I want to learn it. I'll be busy with planting the flowers and making dye.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: And you'll give me some for the eye-dotting ceremony.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Ha, that will depend on the price you offer.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I've got my awesome little clapper who knows everything. He's the one who told me about Pearly. You can't fool me.
steps.female_content: I've got my awesome little clapper who knows everything. She's the one who told me about Pearly. You can't fool me.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Little clapper, pay up! I need to dot the eyes for my extraordinarily gorgeous lion's head!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: First dot on the left eye, brilliant as gold. Second dot on the right eye, shiny as silver...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Third dot on the brow, the lucky star is forever bright above. Fourth dot on the mouth, the world finds peace and prospers...
Bagley has already fallen asleep. OwO closes her eyes drowsily, mumbling something in her dream. She hugs her lion head even more tightly than when she's awake.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Little clapper... I've remembered it...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: That word...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: In... de... pendent...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Zzz... Zzz...
